To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pause of pause neurons associated with quick phases during horizontal nystagmus is, at least partly, produced by inhibitions mediated through long-lead burst neuron area in pontine tegmentum.
the pause of pontine pause neurons during saccade generation is, at least partly, produced by inhibi-tory action mediated through long-lead burst neuron area in cat.
pause neurons are suppressed by stimulation of the pontine long-lead burst neuron region, which is the most likely site of the inhibitory input.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of pause neurons (PN) in the cat pontine reticular formation in the generation of horizontal nystagmus.
the mechanisms that control eye movement in animals.
the neural mechanisms of the vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LLBNs and PNs are both involved in generating the quick phases of horizontal eye movements.
the inhibitory action of the LLBNs to PNs is a major mechanism for producing a pause of PN activity during quick phases of horizontal nystagmus.
pause neurons receive inhibitory input from LLBNs in the cat.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LLBNs, which are located rostral to the EBNs in the pontine reticular formation, are involved in the generation of the quick phases of horizontal nystagmus.
LLBNs are the most likely candidates to be the inhibitory input to PNs.
the pause of PN spikes is produced by the inhibitory action of LLBNs and by the inhibitory actions of the EBNs and the vestibular nuclei.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pause neurons (PN) in the cat receive an inhibitory input from long-lead burst neuron (LLBN) area.
the pause in PN activity is not due to the inhibition from LLBNs, but from the EBNs.
the pause of PNs is not a result of a simple inhibitory action of the EBN area, but is produced by the interaction of excitatory and inhibitory inputs from the EBN and LLBN areas, respectively.
